\textbf{ENEL445 Full Exam Cheat Sheet — Q1 Roy Smith + Q2 Power Systems / Game Theory / LMI}

\section*{Exam Scope / Strategy}

2 h, 2 Qs, 20 marks each. Cheat sheet: A4 double-sided, calculator. **More mathematical**: formulas, derivations, formulations > prose.

**Q1 Roy Smith:** LS/statistics/regularisation; convex sets/functions; cones/PSD/SOCP/SDP; Schur/LMI; MPC/KKT.  
**Q2 Term 2 mixed:** power systems, game theory, LMI + Term 1 math support.

Exam answer pattern: **define variables -> write objective/constraints -> derive/check dimensions -> 1-line interpretation.**

\section*{Core Math Templates}

\subsection*{Matrix Derivatives / Taylor}

For scalar $f(\mathbf x)$:
$$
f(\mathbf x)\approx f(\mathbf c)+\nabla f(\mathbf c)^T(\mathbf x-\mathbf c)+\frac12(\mathbf x-\mathbf c)^TH(\mathbf c)(\mathbf x-\mathbf c).
$$

Quadratic:
$$
f(\mathbf x)=\mathbf x^TA\mathbf x,\quad \nabla f=(A+A^T)\mathbf x,\quad A=A^T\Rightarrow \nabla f=2A\mathbf x.
$$

$$
f(\mathbf x)=\frac12\mathbf x^TA\mathbf x+\mathbf b^T\mathbf x+c,\quad A=A^T
\Rightarrow \nabla f=A\mathbf x+\mathbf b,\ H=A.
$$

PSD/PD:
$$
A\succeq0\Leftrightarrow \mathbf z^TA\mathbf z\ge0\ \forall \mathbf z;\quad
A\succ0\Leftrightarrow \mathbf z^TA\mathbf z>0\ \forall \mathbf z\ne0.
$$
Stationary + $H\succ0$ $\Rightarrow$ strict local min. Convex twice differentiable: $H(x)\succeq0$.

Newton:
$$
\mathbf x_{k+1}=\mathbf x_k-H(\mathbf x_k)^{-1}\nabla f(\mathbf x_k),\quad
\mathbf p=-H^{-1}\nabla f.
$$
If $H\succ0$: $\nabla f^T\mathbf p=-\nabla f^TH^{-1}\nabla f<0$.

Exact line search for quadratic $f=\frac12x^TAx+b^Tx$ along $p$:
$$
\phi(\mu)=f(c+\mu p),\quad
\mu^*=-\frac{p^T(Ac+b)}{p^TAp}.
$$

\subsection*{Lagrangian / KKT}

For $\min f(x)$ s.t. $g_i(x)\le0,\ h_j(x)=0$:
$$
L=f+\sum_i\lambda_i g_i+\sum_j\nu_jh_j,\quad \lambda_i\ge0.
$$
KKT: stationarity $\nabla_xL=0$; primal feasible; dual feasible $\lambda_i\ge0$; complementarity $\lambda_i g_i(x)=0$.  
Bounds: $u\le u_{\max}\Rightarrow u-u_{\max}\le0$; $u\ge u_{\min}\Rightarrow u_{\min}-u\le0$.

Convex + regularity $\Rightarrow$ KKT necessary and sufficient. Nonconvex: usually local/necessary only.

\section*{Q1 Roy: Least Squares}

\subsection*{LS Formulation}

Model:
$$
y=\Phi\theta+\epsilon,\quad r=y-\Phi\theta,\quad
\min_\theta\|y-\Phi\theta\|_2^2.
$$
Normal equations:
$$
\Phi^T\Phi\hat\theta=\Phi^Ty,\quad
\hat\theta=(\Phi^T\Phi)^{-1}\Phi^Ty
$$
if full column rank. Residual orthogonality:
$$
\Phi^T(y-\Phi\hat\theta)=0.
$$
Projection: $\hat y=\Phi\hat\theta=P_\Phi y$, $r\perp \operatorname{col}(\Phi)$.

Watch dimensions: $\Phi:N\times d$, $\theta:d\times1$, $\Phi^T\Phi:d\times d$.

\subsection*{Unbiasedness / Covariance / CI}

Assume fixed $\Phi$, full rank, $E[\epsilon]=0$:
$$
\hat\theta=\theta_0+(\Phi^T\Phi)^{-1}\Phi^T\epsilon
\Rightarrow E[\hat\theta]=\theta_0.
$$
If $\operatorname{Cov}(\epsilon)=\sigma^2I$:
$$
\operatorname{Cov}(\hat\theta)=\sigma^2(\Phi^T\Phi)^{-1}.
$$
Coefficient SE: $\operatorname{se}(\hat\theta_j)=\hat\sigma\sqrt{[(\Phi^T\Phi)^{-1}]_{jj}}$.  
CI: $\hat\theta_j\pm t_{\alpha/2,N-d}\operatorname{se}(\hat\theta_j)$.

CI smaller $\Leftrightarrow$ estimator more stable / lower variance.

\subsection*{BLUE / Weighted LS}

General noise covariance $E[\epsilon\epsilon^T]=R$:
$$
\hat\theta_{\rm BLUE}=(\Phi^TR^{-1}\Phi)^{-1}\Phi^TR^{-1}y,
\quad \operatorname{Cov}=(\Phi^TR^{-1}\Phi)^{-1}.
$$
BLUE minimises **variance among unbiased linear estimators**, not MSE over biased estimators.

Inverse-variance weights for independent unbiased estimates:
$$
\hat\theta_w=\sum_iw_i\hat\theta_i,\quad
\sum_iw_i=1,\quad
w_i=\frac{1/\sigma_i^2}{\sum_j1/\sigma_j^2}.
$$

\subsection*{Bias / Variance / MSE / Metric}

$$
\operatorname{Bias}(\hat\theta)=E[\hat\theta]-\theta,\quad
\operatorname{Var}(\hat\theta)=E[(\hat\theta-E[\hat\theta])^2],
$$
$$
\operatorname{MSE}(\hat\theta)=E[(\hat\theta-\theta)^2].
$$
Derivation:
$$
\hat\theta-\theta
=\big(\hat\theta-E[\hat\theta]\big)+\big(E[\hat\theta]-\theta\big).
$$
$$
\operatorname{MSE}
=E[(\hat\theta-E[\hat\theta])^2]
+2(E[\hat\theta]-\theta)E[\hat\theta-E[\hat\theta]]
+(E[\hat\theta]-\theta)^2
$$
$$
=\operatorname{Var}(\hat\theta)+\operatorname{Bias}(\hat\theta)^2.
$$
Prediction/safety/control: prefer lower variance/stable estimates. Scientific parameter interpretation: bias of a particular coefficient may matter more than total MSE. Metric follows purpose.

\subsection*{Regularisation}

Ridge:
$$
\min_\theta \frac12\|y-\Phi\theta\|_2^2+\frac{\lambda}{2}\|\theta\|_2^2
\Rightarrow
(\Phi^T\Phi+\lambda I)\hat\theta=\Phi^Ty.
$$
Stability: $\lambda I$ lifts small singular/eigenvalues, improves conditioning, lowers variance, adds bias.

Tikhonov:
$$
\min_\theta\|y-\Phi\theta\|^2+\|R\theta\|^2
\Rightarrow(\Phi^T\Phi+R^TR)\theta=\Phi^Ty.
$$
$R$ useful if structured; arbitrary $R$ creates too many hyperparameters.

LASSO: $\|y-\Phi\theta\|^2+\lambda\|\theta\|_1$; sparse, variable selection, no closed form generally.  
Elastic Net: $\lambda_1\|\theta\|_1+\lambda_2\|\theta\|_2^2$; sparse + handles correlated predictors.

Rule: Ridge many weak signals; LASSO few useful signals; Elastic Net correlated/varying signals. Use validation/CV for $\lambda$.

Engineering order: better $\Phi$ first (variables, measurements, experiment design), regularisation second.

\section*{Q1 Roy: Convex Geometry}

Convex set:
$$
x,y\in C,\ \alpha\in[0,1]\Rightarrow \alpha x+(1-\alpha)y\in C.
$$
Cone:
$$
x\in C,\ \gamma\ge0\Rightarrow\gamma x\in C.
$$
Convex cone:
$$
x_i\in C,\ \gamma_i\ge0\Rightarrow \sum_i\gamma_ix_i\in C.
$$

Hyperplane: $\{x\mid a^Tx=b\}$; halfspace $\{x\mid a^Tx\le b\}$. $a$ is normal. One equality removes one degree of freedom.  
Polyhedron: $\{x\mid Ax\le b,\ Cx=d\}$. Test feasible side by substituting a point.

Norm ball: $\{x\mid\|x-x_c\|\le r\}$. Norm cone/SOC:
$$
\mathcal Q^{n+1}=\{(t,x)\mid \|x\|_2\le t\}.
$$
Ellipsoid:
$$
\{x\mid(x-x_c)^TP^{-1}(x-x_c)\le1\},\ P\succ0.
$$

Convex function:
$$
f(\alpha x+(1-\alpha)y)\le\alpha f(x)+(1-\alpha)f(y),
$$
domain must be convex. Strict convex: unique minimiser if exists. Norms are convex.

Quasi-convex:
$$
S_\alpha=\{x\mid f(x)\le\alpha\}\ \text{convex for all }\alpha.
$$
Bisection searches value $\alpha$: feasible $\Rightarrow$ lower upper bound; infeasible $\Rightarrow$ raise lower bound. Armijo/backtracking searches step size $t$ along descent direction $d$:
$$
x^+=x+td,\quad
f(x+td)\le f(x)+ct\nabla f(x)^Td,\quad 0<c<1.
$$
Start $t=1$; if fail, $t\leftarrow\beta t$ ($0<\beta<1$). Bisection = global/value/feasibility; Armijo = local/step/gradient.

Ellipsoid method: keep ellipsoid containing optimum; gradient/subgradient/violated constraint gives halfspace cut; wrap kept half with smaller ellipsoid. Theory/LP polynomial-time proof; not practical first-choice solver.

\section*{Q1/Q2: Cone, SDP, LMI, Schur}

Cone language:
$$
Ax\le b\Leftrightarrow b-Ax\in\mathbb R_+^m.
$$
LMI:
$$
F(x)=F_0+\sum_i x_iF_i\succeq0
$$
is linear/affine in variables and constrained to PSD cone $S_+^n$.

PSD cone:
$$
S_+^n=\{X=X^T\mid X\succeq0\}.
$$
For $2\times2$:
$$
\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{bmatrix}\succeq0
\Leftrightarrow a\ge0,\ c\ge0,\ ac-b^2\ge0.
$$
Example: $\begin{bmatrix}2&x\\x&8\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\Rightarrow16-x^2\ge0\Rightarrow |x|\le4$.

Schur complement:
$$
\begin{bmatrix}Q&S\\S^T&R\end{bmatrix}\succ0,\ R\succ0
\Leftrightarrow Q-SR^{-1}S^T\succ0.
$$
Also with signs:
$$
\begin{bmatrix}Q&S\\S^T&R\end{bmatrix}\preceq0,\ R\prec0
\Leftrightarrow Q-SR^{-1}S^T\preceq0.
$$
Block expansion: $[u^T,v^T]\begin{bmatrix}Q&S\\S^T&R\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=u^TQu+2u^TSv+v^TRv$.

Quadratic constraint to LMI, need $Q\succ0$ not just $Q\succeq0$:
$$
x^TQx+b^Tx+c\le0
\Leftrightarrow
\begin{bmatrix}
c+b^Tx & x^T\\
x & -Q^{-1}
\end{bmatrix}\preceq0.
$$

SOC/norm to LMI:
$$
\|Ax+b\|_2\le c^Tx+d,\ t=c^Tx+d
$$
requires $t\ge0$ and
$$
\begin{bmatrix}
tI & Ax+b\\
(Ax+b)^T & t
\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.
$$

Spectral norm:
$$
\|A(x)\|_2<\gamma
\Leftrightarrow
\begin{bmatrix}\gamma I&A(x)\\A(x)^T&\gamma I\end{bmatrix}\succ0.
$$
Hidden condition $\gamma>0$. Why LMI? every matrix entry affine in $(x,\gamma)$.

Epigraph trick:
$$
\min f(x)\quad\Leftrightarrow\quad \min t\ \text{s.t. } f(x)\le t.
$$
This turns nonlinear objective into constraint plus linear cost.

\subsection*{Lyapunov / Control LMI}

Discrete stability: $x_{k+1}=Ax_k$ stable if $\exists P\succ0$:
$$
A^TPA-P\prec0.
$$
Schur form:
$$
\begin{bmatrix}-P&A^T\\A&-P^{-1}\end{bmatrix}\prec0.
$$
Congruence transform preserves definiteness: $M\prec0$, nonsingular $T$ $\Rightarrow T^TMT\prec0$.

State feedback $u=Kx$, closed loop $A+BK$. Use variable substitution (e.g. $Y=P^{-1}$, $L=KY$) to make inequalities linear in variables.

\section*{Q1 Roy: MPC}

Dynamics:
$$
x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k+Fw_k.
$$
Finite horizon:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_{\{x_i,u_i\}} \quad
& \sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\left[(x_i-r_i)^TQ(x_i-r_i)+u_i^TRu_i\right]
+(x_N-r_N)^TQ_f(x_N-r_N)\\
\text{s.t.}\quad
& x_{i+1}=Ax_i+Bu_i,\ i=0,\dots,N-1,\quad x_0=x_k,\\
& u_{\min}\le u_i\le u_{\max},\quad x_i\in\mathcal X,\quad x_N\in\mathcal X_f.
\end{aligned}
$$

Meaning: $x_k$ state vector; $u_k$ control input; $N$ prediction horizon; $r_i$ reference/target trajectory. $A$ natural dynamics; $B$ input effect; $Q$ tracking/state weight; $R$ control-effort weight. High $Q$/low $R$ = aggressive; high $R$ = smooth/conservative.

MPC loop: measure/estimate $x_k$ -> optimise future trajectory -> apply first $u_k$ -> repeat. Linear dynamics + quadratic cost + linear bounds $\Rightarrow$ QP after stacking:
$z=[x_0^T,\dots,x_N^T,u_0^T,\dots,u_{N-1}^T]^T$, $J=\frac12z^THz+f^Tz+\text{const}$, $Gz\le h,\ Ez=e$. $H$ from $Q,R,Q_f$; $f$ from reference. Nonlinear dynamics/cost/constraints or integer vars break standard QP.

Explicit MPC one-step:
$$
J=x_{k+1}^TQx_{k+1}+u_k^TRu_k,\quad x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k.
$$
Substitute: $J=x_k^TA^TQAx_k+2x_k^TA^TQBu_k+u_k^T(B^TQB+R)u_k$.  
Let scalar input $H=B^TQB+R>0$, $g=B^TQA$. Interior:
$2gx_k+2Hu_k=0\Rightarrow u_k^*=-H^{-1}gx_k$.  
Bounds:
$u^*(x)=\min\{u_{\max},\max\{u_{\min},-H^{-1}gx\}\}$.
Piecewise affine controller; active constraints define regions.

\section*{Q2 Power Systems}

\subsection*{Economic Dispatch / Pricing}

ED:
$$
\min_{P_{G_i}}\sum_i C_i(P_{G_i}),\quad
\sum_iP_{G_i}=P_D,\quad P_i^{\min}\le P_{G_i}\le P_i^{\max}.
$$
No active limits/no losses:
$$
\frac{dC_i}{dP_{G_i}}=\lambda.
$$
With losses:
$$
P_D+P_L(P_G)-\sum_iP_{G_i}=0,\quad
L_i=\frac1{1-\partial P_L/\partial P_{G_i}},
$$
optimal:
$$
L_iIC_i(P_{G_i})=\lambda.
$$

Uniform price: all accepted generators paid marginal clearing price. Pay-as-bid: each paid own bid; more strategic bidding.

ED KKT with bounds: $L=C+\lambda(P_D-\sum_iP_i)+\sum_i\mu_i^-(P_i^{\min}-P_i)+\sum_i\mu_i^+(P_i-P_i^{\max})$.  
Stationarity: $C_i'(P_i)-\lambda-\mu_i^-+\mu_i^+=0$; complementarity: $\mu_i^-(P_i^{\min}-P_i)=0$, $\mu_i^+(P_i-P_i^{\max})=0$.

LMP intuition: no congestion/loss $\Rightarrow$ same marginal price everywhere. Congestion/losses make bus prices differ; shadow prices on line limits enter local marginal cost.

\subsection*{OPF Types}

OPF = Optimal Power Flow: choose generation/control variables to minimise cost subject to power-flow equations and operating limits.  
ED: generation cost + total balance, ignores network.  
DC OPF: linear active-power flows and line limits; fast real-time approximation.  
AC OPF: full $P,Q,V,\theta$ nonlinear AC equations; accurate but large/nonconvex.  
SC-OPF: base case + contingencies (outage/disturbance cases: line/gen/transformer outage), much larger.

AC OPF hard: many vars/constraints; $\sin,\cos$; nonlinear/nonconvex equalities; real-time; SC constraints multiply cases.  
Mitigate: DC OPF, linearisation, piecewise loss approximation, warm start, interior-point, decomposition, contingency screening, AC feasibility check after DC OPF.

Interior-point barrier:
$$
\begin{gathered}
\min f(x)\ \text{s.t. }g_i(x)\le0,\ h(x)=0\\
\Rightarrow\ 
\min \left[f(x)-\mu\sum_i\log(-g_i(x))\right]
\ \text{s.t. }h(x)=0.
\end{gathered}
$$

Scaling:
$$
t_2/t_1\approx(N_2/N_1)^3,\quad
t_{AC}\approx5t_{DC}(N_{AC}/N_{DC})^3.
$$

\subsection*{DC Power Flow / DC OPF}

Assumptions: $V_i\approx1$ p.u.; ignore $Q$; small angles; lossless/negligible resistance.
$$
\sin(\theta_i-\theta_j)\approx\theta_i-\theta_j,\quad
P_{ij}=B_{ij}(\theta_i-\theta_j).
$$
DC OPF is DC **approximation** of AC grid, not DC electrical grid.

\subsection*{State Estimation}

General:
$$
z=h(x)+e,\quad
\min_x(z-h(x))^TR^{-1}(z-h(x)).
$$
Equal variances: $\min_x\|z-h(x)\|_2^2$. Linear $h(x)=Hx$:
$$
\hat x=(H^TH)^{-1}H^Tz,\quad
\hat x_W=(H^TR^{-1}H)^{-1}H^TR^{-1}z.
$$
Need reference angle because only angle differences observable.

DC SE template: measurements
$$
z=[P_{12}^m,P_{13}^m,P_{32}^m]^T,\quad P_{ij}=B_{ij}(\theta_i-\theta_j).
$$
Set $\theta_1=0$, $x=[\theta_2,\theta_3]^T$:
$$
H=\begin{bmatrix}
-B_{12}&0\\
0&-B_{13}\\
-B_{32}&B_{32}
\end{bmatrix},\quad
\min_x\|z-Hx\|_2^2.
$$

AC NLS:
$$
P_{ij}=V_iV_jB_{ij}\sin(\theta_i-\theta_j),
$$
$$
Q_{ij}=V_i(V_i-V_j\cos(\theta_i-\theta_j))B_{ij}.
$$
Choose state, e.g. $x=[V_1,V_2,V_3,\theta_2,\theta_3]^T$ with $\theta_1=0$; stack measurements $z$ and model $h(x)$:
$$
\min_x\|z-h(x)\|_2^2
$$
or weighted. If unknown parameter e.g. $B_{32}$, include it in $x$.

Per unit: $P_{\rm pu}=P_{\rm actual}/S_{\rm base}$.

\section*{Q2 Game Theory}

Game theory: multiple players, each controls own strategy and payoff; result is equilibrium, not necessarily global optimum.

Payoff matrix method:
Reward matrix: larger is better; cost/sentence matrix: smaller is better. For each column mark row player's BR; for each row mark column player's BR; overlap = Nash equilibrium. NE is strategy profile, payoff is separate.

Nash equilibrium:
$$
s^*=(s_1^*,...,s_n^*)\quad
u_i(s_i^*,s_{-i}^*)\ge u_i(s_i,s_{-i}^*)\ \forall s_i,\forall i.
$$
No player can improve by unilateral deviation. NE $\ne$ social optimum.

Dominant strategy: best regardless of opponent. Dominated: worse than another strategy for all opponent actions.

Prisoner's dilemma: dominant defect for both; NE $(D,D)$; social optimum $(C,C)$; individual rationality can be collectively inefficient.

Maximax: choose best possible payoff (optimistic).  
Maximin: choose best worst-case payoff (conservative).  
Minimax: minimise maximum loss/regret (robust).

Zero-sum: $u_1=-u_2$. Simultaneous: Cournot. Sequential: Stackelberg. Dynamic: multiple stages/time.

Best response example:
$$
U_1=12x_1-x_1^2-x_1x_2,\quad
\frac{\partial U_1}{\partial x_1}=12-2x_1-x_2=0
$$
$$
BR_1(x_2)=6-\frac{x_2}{2},\quad
BR_2(x_1)=6-\frac{x_1}{2}.
$$
Solve simultaneous equations for Nash.

Mixed strategy $2\times2$: make opponent indifferent. If row payoff is $\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix}$ and column plays top-column prob $q$, solve
$qa+(1-q)b=qc+(1-q)d$. Do analogous equation for column player.

\section*{Fast Classification / Common Traps}

LP: linear objective, linear constraints.  
QP: quadratic objective, linear constraints. OLS is QP; constrained LS no normal-equation closed form.  
QCQP: quadratic objective + quadratic constraints.  
SOCP: norm cone constraints $\|Ax+b\|\le c^Tx+d$.  
SDP/LMI: affine matrix constrained PSD.

Convex optimisation standard:
$$
\min f_0(x),\quad f_i(x)\le0,\quad Ax=b
$$
with convex $f_i$, affine equality. Nonlinear equality generally nonconvex.

LP standard form reminders: convert max to min by negating; $x$ free $\Rightarrow x=x^+-x^-$, $x^\pm\ge0$; $\le$ add slack; $\ge$ subtract surplus.

Formulation checklist: decision variables? known data? objective? constraints? dimensions? linear/nonlinear/convex? solve or only formulate?

Common mistakes:
- use $\Phi\Phi^T$ instead of $\Phi^T\Phi$;
- forget reference bus angle in power SE;
- call DC OPF a DC grid;
- say AC OPF hard only because large; also nonlinear/nonconvex;
- forget $t\ge0$ in norm/SOC;
- mix KKT sign conventions;
- treat Nash as social optimum;
- Schur complement with wrong sign/definite block.

\section*{Extra Calculation Templates}

\subsection*{Quadratic ED}
If $C_i(P_i)=a_iP_i^2+b_iP_i+c_i$ and no active limits/losses:
$$
2a_iP_i+b_i=\lambda
\Rightarrow
P_i=\frac{\lambda-b_i}{2a_i},\quad
\sum_iP_i=P_D.
$$
If computed $P_i$ violates limits, fix it at bound and redispatch remaining demand.

\subsection*{Generic OPF Forms}
DC OPF:
$$
\min_{P_G,\theta}\sum_iC_i(P_{G_i})
$$
$$
\text{s.t. } P_G-P_D=B_{\rm bus}\theta,\quad
|B_{ij}(\theta_i-\theta_j)|\le F_{ij}^{\max},\quad
P_i^{\min}\le P_{G_i}\le P_i^{\max}.
$$
AC OPF:
$$
\min_{P_G,Q_G,V,\theta}\sum_iC_i(P_{G_i})
$$
s.t. nonlinear AC power balance, flow equations, voltage bounds, gen $P/Q$ bounds, line limits. Nonconvex due to AC equality constraints.

SC-OPF:
$$
\text{base-case constraints}+\text{constraints for each contingency }c\in\mathcal C.
$$

\subsection*{Schur Mini-Checks}
Ellipsoid membership:
$$
(x-c)^TP^{-1}(x-c)\le1
\Leftrightarrow
\begin{bmatrix}
1&(x-c)^T\\
x-c&P
\end{bmatrix}\succeq0,\ P\succ0.
$$
Scalar quadratic $ax^2+2bx+c\le0$, $a>0$:
$$
\begin{bmatrix}
c+2bx & x\\
x & -1/a
\end{bmatrix}\preceq0.
$$
Block diagonal LMIs:
$$
F_i(x)\succeq0\ \forall i
\Leftrightarrow
\operatorname{diag}(F_1(x),...,F_m(x))\succeq0.
$$

\subsection*{LMI Linearity Test}
Allowed entries: $3x_1-2x_2+\gamma+5$.  
Not LMI if entries contain $x_1x_2$, $x^2$, $1/x$, $\sin x$, or decision variable inverse.  
Products with fixed matrices are OK: $A_0+x_1A_1+x_2A_2$.

\subsection*{Payoff Matrix Fast Marking}
Reward matrix: mark max. Cost/sentence matrix: mark min.  
For each column mark row player's BR; for each row mark column player's BR; double-marked cell = NE. Multiple double marks possible. No pure NE possible.

\subsection*{Term 1 Support}
Infinity norm:
$$
\|x\|_\infty=\max_i|x_i|.
$$
Directional derivative:
$$
x=c+\mu p,\quad
f(c+\mu p)\approx f(c)+\mu\nabla f(c)^Tp.
$$
At local min, arbitrary $p$ gives $\nabla f(c)^Tp=0\ \forall p\Rightarrow\nabla f(c)=0$.

Slackness: inequality inactive $\Rightarrow g_i(x)<0,\lambda_i=0$; active $\Rightarrow g_i(x)=0,\lambda_i$ may be positive. SQP handles active-set combinatorics by solving successive QP approximations.

\subsection*{High-Value Extras}
Continuous-time Lyapunov stability: $\dot x=Ax$ stable if $\exists P\succ0$ with $A^TP+PA\prec0$. Lyapunov equation: pick $Q\succ0$, solve $A^TP+PA=-Q$.

Stackelberg game: follower first-order condition $\Rightarrow$ best response $BR_F(s_L)$; substitute into leader payoff; optimise leader variable.

LP geometry: linear objective contour is a line/plane; optimum of bounded LP occurs at a vertex. QP contour is ellipse/parabola; optimum may occur inside feasible polytope, not necessarily vertex.

KKT active-set shortcut: inactive constraint $\Rightarrow\lambda=0$; active bound substitutes variable at limit, then use stationarity to check multiplier sign.

Gradient-free: use when gradients unavailable/unreliable/noisy/discontinuous/expensive, black-box simulations/experiments, or discrete variables. Nelder-Mead: simplex of $n+1$ points, reflection/expansion/contraction/shrink. Pattern search: poll directions, accept improvement else reduce step.

\subsection*{Exam Triage}
If asked "formulate": do not solve; define $x,z,h,H,R$, objective and constraints.
